Date: 2025-05-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Evelyn Park (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Content), Rachel Moreno (FirstLight Producer), Amit Shah (FirstLight CTO), Lina Torres (FirstLight Head of ML)
Recording: Yes (podcast/pre-approval)
Notes: Marketing interview / customer testimonial recording; intended for a short form podcast and a written case study
summary: Informal podcast-style customer interview capturing FirstLight Media's experience migrating inference for audio-to-text and personalization features to Redwood Inference. Discussed reasons for choosing Redwood, performance and cost tradeoffs, Dedicated vs Hosted, security/compliance needs, and expected business outcomes. Ended with agreement to circulate draft case study and benchmarks and schedule publication approvals.
topics: Intro & backstory; Why Redwood; technical migration details (latency, batching, KV cache), security & compliance (SOC2, SSO, KMS), creative/publishing use case, metrics and outcomes, next steps for case study and podcast publication
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samir (Host - Redwood): Hey everyone, welcome to a short customer chat — thanks so much for joining, Rachel, Amit, Lina, and of course Evelyn and Jordan from our team. We're recording this as a short podcast and a case study so quick note: we'll share the draft before publishing. Um, shall we — Rachel do you want to kick off with a quick intro to FirstLight?

[00:00:34] Rachel (FirstLight Producer): Yeah hi everyone, thanks for having us. I'm Rachel, I produce content for FirstLight Media, uh we run several podcast networks, live audio events, and we recently launched a personalization layer that suggests clips to listeners. We work with a small ML infra team — Amit and Lina — who'll talk about the tech choices.

[00:01:05] Amit (CTO): Hey all. Quick context: historically we used a mix of third-party ASR APIs and an internal monolith for personalization. Cost and latency were getting out of hand as catalogs grew, and we wanted more control over data residency and logging for advertisers. We started a POC with Redwood last year.

[00:01:35] Lina (Head of ML): For us the big things were throughput during live drops, and being able to run custom models for speaker diarization. We love low-latency for clip generation, and cost predictability was also critical.

[00:02:02] Samir: Great. Could you describe the moment where you decided to move from the old stack to Redwood? What triggered the POC?

[00:02:20] Amit: Right, so during a big release last Q3 we saw a spike in transcription costs and latency hit 1.2 seconds average which is too slow for our UX. Our infra team couldn't guarantee <500 ms tail latency. We evaluated a few options — more reserved capacity on our previous vendor, building our own inference layer, or trying Redwood. Redwood came in with a clear throughput profile and the Dedicated option appealed because of predictable capacity.

[00:03:05] Evelyn (Redwood SE): I'll add — during the POC we focused on two things: sustained throughput for concurrent live streams, and token-level cost analysis on our optimizer. We ran a small benchmark that matched your peak waveform lengths.

[00:03:35] Lina: The benchmark results were pretty eye-opening. We saw cost per 1k tokens drop by about 35% on the dedicated pools compared to our previous setup, and latency 95th dropped from 1.2s to ~420ms on a good run. There was some variability depending on sequence length and batching config.

[00:04:10] Rachel: That was huge for us — clips feel more immediate and engagement went up. We also liked that Redwood provided those dashboards — Jordan, you pulled screenshots during the POC, right?

[00:04:29] Jordan (Content): Yep — I grabbed the per-route latency graphs, token-cost breakdowns, and the KV cache heatmaps. We used them in the internal pitch deck for the execs.

[00:04:48] Samir: There are always questions about security for marketing stories. Tell us what the security conversation looked like with your legal and infra teams.

[00:05:03] Amit: Legal wanted SOC2 scope and audit logs, and infra wanted KMS integration for keys and the ability to run in our VPC. Redwood's private offering and SSO support checked most boxes. There was a short back-and-forth about retention policies — we tightened the retention to align with advertiser contracts.

[00:05:33] Evelyn: We also provided sample audit logs and helped map events to your SIEM during the POC; there was a small config change to keep the logs in a customer-controlled bucket. Note — sometimes the transcriptions in our docs refer to K-V cash instead of KV cache, so apologies for typos in auto-docs.

[00:05:56] Lina: (laughs) yeah the KV cash confusion was funny. But in practice that K-V cache change made a big difference for repeated snippets, and reduced the compute needed for personalization.

[00:06:20] Samir: For listeners who are more technical — did you run into model compatibility or quantization issues when moving custom diarization models?

[00:06:38] Lina: We did. Our model was originally tuned in fp32 and used some ops that weren't in the default kernel set. Redwood's team helped with kernel selection and a slightly different compilation path; we did a small re-train/convert to a quantized-friendly version. There were some initial output differences but the evals showed parity on speaker separation.

[00:07:05] Evelyn: Right — we recommended a 4-bit quantization profile for the bottleneck layers and kept the attention kernels native. That combination kept latency low without perceptible quality drop. We documented the changes in the benchmark sheet.

[00:07:31] Amit: A practical note: the canary rollout tooling was super helpful for us. We rolled the new model to 10% traffic, monitored quality regression with a small eval set, and then ramped. That reduced risk for shows with strict advertiser SLAs.

[00:07:59] Rachel: Can we talk about creative outcomes? What changed for show producers and the listener experience?

[00:08:12] Lina: Clips are auto-generated faster so editorial teams can push promos in near real-time. Personalization improved clickthrough on recommended clips by about 12% in early tests.

[00:08:28] Rachel: Yeah advertisers were happy because we could provide faster turnarounds and more targeted promos. That helped revenue per episode.

[00:08:41] Samir: Nice. Were there any tradeoffs you had to accept? Latency vs cost, or management overhead?

[00:08:51] Amit: The main tradeoff was upfront engineering work — converting models, integrating KMS, and configuring Dedicated pools. But post-rollout the ops overhead decreased; we actually reduced our manual scaling runbooks because Redwood's autoscaling and burst options handled sudden spikes.

[00:09:18] Jordan: Also the visibility into token-level cost changed our product decisions — we started batching some lower-priority tasks into off-peak windows.

[00:09:33] Samir: Nice detail. Listeners might ask about pricing — without getting into exact numbers, how would you describe the impact on unit economics?

[00:09:44] Lina: We can't share exact vendor rates, but the combination of smarter batching, KV cache, and Dedicated pricing reduced our per-clip cost materially — that's why the 35% number came up in the POC, and it held in production with tweaks.

[00:10:05] Amit: Another note — we kept some fallback to hosted endpoints for non-critical workloads to balance costs during low utilization. That hybrid routing approach was easy to configure.

[00:10:22] Samir: Great — let's talk timeline and approvals for the case study and podcast. Rachel, what's your schedule?

[00:10:33] Rachel: We want to publish the short podcast episode the week of May 26th, pending legal approval. I'll need the draft transcript and case study by May 13th to circulate internally. Also we'll want the benchmark spreadsheet for the appendix.

[00:10:52] Samir: Okay we'll do that. Evelyn, you'll send the benchmarks?

[00:10:59] Evelyn: Yep I'll package the benchmark sheet and include notes on which runs were Dedicated vs Hosted and the quantization profile we used.

[00:11:12] Lina: Quick question — will the quoted numbers be anonymized or full?

[00:11:18] Rachel: We usually run them by legal; FirstLight is fine with headline metrics but the appendix can keep raw numbers redacted until sign-off.

[00:11:30] Samir: Perfect. Anything else from the team before we wrap?

[00:11:36] Amit: One ask — can Redwood share a short blurb about the Dedicated SLA we committed to? Our sales ops wants clarity for the case study.

[00:11:45] Samir: Yes we'll put an SLA summary in the doc.

[00:11:49] Jordan: Also I'll drop the per-route graphs and a short GIF of the dashboard into the deck link.

[00:11:56] Rachel: Thanks all. This was great. We're excited.

[00:12:02] Samir: Awesome. To recap — we'll share: 1) case study draft and podcast MP3 for review by May 13th (Samir), 2) benchmark spreadsheets and technical notes (Evelyn) by May 12th, 3) FirstLight to confirm legal approvals and publish date by May 16th (Rachel). We'll also include a short SLA blurb and per-route graphs.

[00:12:28] Rachel: Sounds good, thanks everyone.

[00:12:32] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up over email with the doc links. Bye!

Note: transcript contains occasional auto-transcription artifacts (names and acronyms) and is lightly edited for readability.
